wiki_text: On 23 February 2026, Chile's Comité de Ministros (Committee of Ministers) rejected the outstanding invalidation requests filed against the Terminal Marítimo GNL Penco-Lirquén and ratified the project's favorable Environmental Qualification Resolution (RCA), reaffirming the environmental approval originally granted in October 2023. The project, held by GM Energy SpA, envisages an offshore island-type LNG reception, storage and regasification terminal connected via a 2.5 km submarine pipeline and a 13 km onshore pipeline to the regional gas distribution system, with a stated capacity to supply about 15 million m3/day of natural gas and an estimated investment of US$165 million. Despite the reaffirmed permit, GM Energy has not confirmed near-term execution, stating its current focus is on renewable-energy (solar and storage) projects; the terminal therefore remained at the proposal stage as of mid-2026.
